The movement into the wallet and the 35-unit debit represent different events. If another 10 is later used for shipping, the expected remaining balance would be five. These are illustrative amounts. Save the real recorded entries and account for any separately listed adjustment, refund or payment directly through another provider.

sections.heading: Follow up on a mismatch safely
paragraphs: If the provider shows a completed transfer but the account shows no corresponding wallet credit, record the time, amount, currency and reference. If the wallet shows a debit but the order remains unpaid, capture that order status as a separate observation. Contact official support privately with the specific mismatch and keep sensitive payment credentials out of screenshots. Avoid repeating a payment just to see whether the first one worked before reviewing the original transaction and its status.

sections.heading: Draw the difference between funding and spending
paragraphs: A wallet makes sense only if you can tell when it gained funds and when those funds were used. Treat the external payment provider, wallet and seller order as three distinct records. A top-up may reduce the provider balance while increasing the platform balance. An order paid using that wallet may reduce the platform balance without creating a second external charge. Compare amounts on both sides of each event. The same money can appear in two records for accounting reasons without representing two separate purchases.

For example, imagine a buyer funds a wallet with 80 units, spends 50 on merchandise and has 30 left. The merchandise cost is 50 and the unused wallet balance is 30. The temporary cash outflow from the external account is 80. All three figures can be correct because they answer different questions. If the buyer later pays 20 of freight from the same balance, merchandise and freight together account for 70 while 10 remains. Label the measure you are reporting before calling the whole deposit the cost of the goods.

sections.heading: Check the requirements of the payment you are about to make
paragraphs: Open the order or parcel checkout first and confirm which charge is due. An unpaid seller order needs merchandise payment; an unpaid international parcel needs freight payment. A previous wallet top-up may supply funds but does not tell you which of those obligations has been settled. Verify the payment status after completing the intended transaction. If both the order and wallet records are visible, check that the item identifier and amount match the action you just took.

Read the method options displayed for the actual transaction and any current conditions. A method available for one buyer or for one payment stage may be unavailable for another configuration. A promotional wallet balance could also have specific rules. If those rules affect whether you can pay the intended charge or recover unused funds, obtain the terms before topping up. Keep a screenshot of the relevant non-sensitive conditions as they appeared when you decided; an advertising headline alone may omit important details.

sections.heading: Separate authorization, completion and refund in your records
paragraphs: A payment provider may show a pending entry before it becomes posted, expires or changes state. Use the provider's own status terminology and the platform's order status rather than treating every pending line as a completed charge. If an order remains unpaid, first determine whether the external transaction completed and whether a wallet credit or platform payment was recorded. Capture the time and identifiers while the issue is fresh. Avoid repeatedly initiating the same payment without understanding the state of the first attempt.

A refund creates a further pair of questions: did the seller or platform approve it, and where was the money credited? An account balance increase differs from a reversal to an external payment method. Look for the destination and transaction reference in the actual refund record. If you were expecting a card credit but see a wallet credit, ask about the specific transaction terms and history instead of assuming the amount disappeared. Keep approval and posted credit as separate milestones until the records match.

sections.heading: Think about currency before comparing totals
paragraphs: Write original amounts with their currencies. If a provider converts the transaction into your account currency, retain both the purchase amount and the posted amount. A conversion can change the numerical value even when the original platform charge was correct. When using one currency for a budget spreadsheet, use a consistent method: either record the actual provider-posted amount or clearly label an estimate with the date and rate basis. If you convert a platform display figure and also import the posted external amount, you may accidentally count the same expense twice.

Bonuses, refunds and balances introduce similar bookkeeping questions. A promotional credit may have a different eligibility or withdrawal status from cash-funded balance. If the account displays them separately, keep that distinction. Never assume that every visible balance can be taken out or used for every charge. CNShopper's FAQs direct buyers to check current wallet and withdrawal terms. Use those transaction-specific conditions when deciding how much to deposit, especially if you have no immediate use for the remainder.

sections.heading: Send one actionable payment-support request
paragraphs: For a missing wallet credit, provide the official support team with the top-up reference, provider transaction status, amount, currency and approximate time. For a wallet debit that did not settle an order, give the wallet transaction and the unpaid order or parcel identifier. For a suspected duplicate external payment, identify both posted references and explain why one order appears to have been paid twice. These are three different investigations. A note that says only “my payment failed” leaves support unsure which record to inspect.

Redact complete card numbers, security codes, passwords and unrelated bank activity. Use the platform's official support path, and retain its case number and response. When the issue resolves, update your own ledger with the actual result: wallet credited, order paid, payment reversed, or another documented outcome. Keeping this record alongside your merchandise and freight payments restores a clear picture of what was spent on the goods and which funds remain available for a future purchase.

sections.heading: Carry forward only the usable balance
paragraphs: Before the next purchase, open the current wallet screen and check which portion remains usable for the intended order. Do not rely on a previous reconciliation after a refund, promotion or partial freight payment has occurred. If you decide to top up again, record what the extra funds are for and verify the new credit before using them. This creates a clean link between the earlier order, any money still available and the next payment without turning a wallet deposit into an unexplained second merchandise expense.

faq.q: I already bought the product myself. How do I forward it?
faq.a: Use the forwarding flow to copy the current warehouse details and pre-alert the domestic tracking number. Once the matching package arrives, review it for international shipment.

faq.q: What does the CNShopper forwarding form ask me to enter?
faq.a: The form requests the domestic tracking number, package name, total item value in USD and quantity. Use the contents associated with that physical parcel.

faq.q: Can I submit a batch of forwarding pre-alerts?
faq.a: The forwarding form offers a downloadable bulk template and import. Match each tracking reference to the relevant package before importing.

faq.q: Should I post my China tracking number publicly for help?
faq.a: Keep it private. CNShopper identifies this number as a means of proving ownership of a forwarded parcel, so use private official support for matching issues.

faq.q: Why do I have separate product and freight payments?
faq.a: The first payment generally covers the item and applicable local charges. The later payment covers the international parcel after warehouse details become available.

faq.q: Does a wallet top-up mean my order is paid?
faq.a: Funding a balance and using it at checkout are separate actions. Check the individual order's payment status and the wallet transaction history.

faq.q: How can I find the payment methods available for my purchase?
faq.a: Check the live payment page for that order and review its amounts and terms. Methods and wallet options may vary.

faq.q: How can I estimate freight before warehouse arrival?
faq.a: Use the shipping estimator with the destination and plausible package measurements or weight as requested. Update the estimate once the warehouse has actual details.

faq.q: Why does a lightweight product produce a high shipping estimate?
faq.a: Parcel size also affects international freight. A light, rigid item can occupy a large box, and the selected line's pricing and destination also matter.

faq.q: Can I consolidate items purchased from different sellers?
faq.a: Eligible items registered in your warehouse account can be selected together. Review the available routes and each item's suitability before submitting.

faq.q: Do I have to send all stored items at once?
faq.a: You can select some items for shipment and leave others in storage, subject to the deadlines and terms that apply to each item.

faq.q: Will removing a shoebox always make shipping cheaper?
faq.a: Packaging removal may be available, but the final result depends on the packed parcel and route. Decide first whether the original box is needed for protection or resale condition.

faq.q: How should I handle a fragile item in a mixed parcel?
faq.a: Ask whether the item needs protective packing or separate shipment and specify the packaging to retain. Compare the suitable options before consolidating.

faq.q: When does eligible free warehouse storage normally start?
faq.a: CNShopper says it usually begins when the item is received and registered at the warehouse. Use the date and remaining storage shown for that specific item.

faq.q: Does an advertised 90-day storage period give me 90 days to return an item?
faq.a: No. Eligible free storage can be up to 90 days, while seller and after-sales deadlines can be substantially shorter. Review the item as soon as QC is available.

faq.q: What can I check in CNShopper QC photographs?
faq.a: Look for visible features such as labels, color, accessible package contents, quantity and obvious damage. A photo cannot settle a detail outside the frame.

faq.q: Does warehouse QC certify authenticity or test all functions?
faq.a: CNShopper describes these images as a visual inspection. Its terms exclude authentication, laboratory certification and complete functional checks.

faq.q: My China tracking number says delivered. Is it at my overseas address?
faq.a: Check the destination. Delivery under the seller's domestic reference generally refers to the China warehouse; the international parcel has a separate shipment record.

faq.q: When should I expect an international tracking reference?
faq.a: CNShopper says it is usually generated after the international parcel is processed and handed to the provider. Look in the submitted parcel record.

faq.q: What helps support resolve a wrong-variant request?
faq.a: Provide the order number, seller option selected, warehouse evidence and the exact difference. Contact support before submitting the item for international freight.

faq.q: Can I count on returning a customized item?
faq.a: The return policy lists personalized or customized goods among items that may be ineligible. Verify the specific seller terms before purchasing.
